name: Wang Dawei
current_role: Co-founder and major shareholder of Shenzhen Gongjin Electronics (603118.SH); former chairman (board reorganised Feb 2026 under Tangshan SASAC control)
profile: Wang Dawei (汪大维) co-founded Shenzhen Gongjin Electronics, a broadband/network-equipment contract manufacturer (PON, Wi-Fi APs, DSL, set-top boxes, switches, servers), with Tang Fonan. He was long-time chairman. In late 2025 Tangshan Industrial Holding (Tangshan SASAC) agreed to take control, and in Feb 2026 Wang Jianxiang became chairman.
interesting_fact: Gongjin is nicknamed a 'little Huawei' in the industry; by 2025 it had shipped 400G data-center switches in volume, trial-produced 800G switches and produced over 30,000 servers, including AI servers.
notes: Hurun wealth is shared with his wife Wang Danhua. Control of Gongjin has passed to Tangshan state capital, so his current operating role is unclear; very low public profile. Data-center angle: the company's server and switch push, plus the new owner's wind assets in Chifeng.

name: Han Fang
current_role: Chairman and actual controller, Nacity Property Service Group (南都物业, 603506.SH), Hangzhou
profile: Han Fang (韩芳, b. 1971) joined Zhejiang Nandu Real Estate in 1993 and rose to group vice president. She took over its property-management arm, turned it profitable, and in 2018 made Nacity the first property-services company listed on China's A-share market. She controls about 57% of Nacity and is pushing into smart services and robotics ('Nacity Robotics').
interesting_fact: Under her, Nacity became mainland China's first A-share-listed property-management company. She started at Nandu Real Estate as an ordinary employee and worked up to running the business.
deep_cut_fact: She was in the first graduating class of the Hong Kong Polytechnic University's International Real Estate (IRE) master's programme. She chairs the Zhejiang University-PolyU joint centre alumni association, and her personal motto is 'think carefully, discern clearly; move steadily, go far' (慎思明辨，行稳致远).
notes: Not to be confused with Seazen's 新城悦服务 (a similar English name; its chairman is Qi Xiaoming). She was named a Zhejiang Women Entrepreneur of the Year (12th edition). Best route is Nacity investor relations.

name: Ruan Shouguo
current_role: Founder/former owner of Anhui Chaohu Haixing Cable Group; shareholder in Beijing Dinghan Technology (300011.SZ) since 2014 (current role not confirmed)
profile: Ruan Shouguo (阮寿国) and Ruan Renyi owned 100% of Anhui Chaohu Haixing Cable Group, which makes rail-vehicle and special cables. In 2014 they sold it to Beijing Dinghan Technology, a rail-transit electrical equipment maker, for about 91.6 million new Dinghan shares and also took part in its private placement. Dinghan is now controlled by Guangzhou state capital (Guangzhou Industrial Investment).
interesting_fact: Haixing Cable was folded into Dinghan's rail-transit group and continues as its cable arm (e.g. Wuhu Dinghan, making EU/GB-standard rail-vehicle cables). The 2014 share-swap made the Ruans among Dinghan's largest shareholders.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal web presence found. Hurun wealth is shared with Ruan Renyi. Dinghan founder Gu Qingwei is a different person. Dinghan also sells rail energy-storage and liquid-cooling thermal-management systems, which is the closest energy angle.

name: Valeriy Khoroshkovskyi
current_role: Private investor/businessman, based abroad since about 2014 (no confirmed current corporate title)
profile: Kyiv-born (1969) Ukrainian businessman and politician. He made money in metal trading and banking (sold his Ukrsotsbank stake to Victor Pinchuk in 2004), briefly ran Evraz in 2006, and controlled Inter Media Group until selling it to Dmytro Firtash in 2013. He was economy minister, head of the State Customs Service, SBU chief (2010-12), finance minister and First Deputy PM (2012), and has lived outside Ukraine since about 2014.
interesting_fact: In 2005 he bought 61% of Inter, Ukraine's most-watched TV channel, for about $250m and built it into U.A. Inter Media Group before selling to Firtash in 2013.
deep_cut_fact: He became Ukraine's Minister of Economy and European Integration in December 2002 at about 33, after one term (1998-2002) as a Verkhovna Rada deputy.
notes: Politically sensitive figure (former SBU head under Yanukovych). Ukrainian media report that 2025 court orders froze some of his Ukrainian assets in a tax case. Lives abroad; no published contact channel found. Not a natural podcast guest; journalist discretion advised.

name: Liu Tongbo
current_role: CEO and Director, Sunlands Technology Group (NYSE: STG), Beijing
profile: Liu Tongbo (刘通博) joined Sunlands, the online adult-education company founded by Peng Ou, in 2009 straight out of Tsinghua University. He has been CEO since January 2015 and a director since August 2017, and led the company through its 2018 NYSE IPO. Sunlands offers online degree and diploma-prep and professional-certification courses in China.
interesting_fact: Sunlands listed on the NYSE in March 2018 as one of China's largest online post-secondary and professional education platforms. Liu became CEO about six years after joining as a new graduate.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a bachelor's degree in applied mathematics from Tsinghua University and joined Sunlands right after graduating in 2009, so he has spent his whole career at the company.
notes: The company founder and chairman is Peng Ou, not Liu, although some profiles call Liu a founder. Liu gave interviews to China Daily (2018). Best route is Sunlands IR, which also handles media.

name: Mark N Lampert
current_role: Founder and General Partner, BVF Partners L.P. (Biotechnology Value Fund), San Francisco
profile: Mark Lampert founded BVF Partners in 1993. The San Francisco firm is one of the longest-running biotech-focused investors and holds large stakes in companies such as Kymera, MoonLake, Palvella and 4D Molecular Therapeutics. Before BVF he was a VP at Oppenheimer & Co. and had worked at Cambridge NeuroScience, G.D. Searle and BCG. He has been active in biotech since 1984.
interesting_fact: Before BVF he founded Biotechnology Royalty Corp., an early attempt to pool university biotech patent royalties, long before royalty funds became a mainstream asset class.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Ann Arbor, Michigan, earned an A.B. with honors in chemistry at Harvard, and is a founding donor to GiveDirectly, the charity that sends cash directly to people living in poverty, as well as the Lampert-Byrd Foundation.
notes: Spoke at the Invest for Kids Chicago conference (2018, listed again as a 2026 speaker). An unverified TheOrg listing puts him on the board of International Lifeline Fund. BVF's website is behind Cloudflare and no published contact was retrieved. Best route is probably via BVF Partners in San Francisco. Biotech investor, so a weak fit with energy/data centers.

name: Tan Changan
current_role: Founder of the Tan Yutou (谭鱼头) hotpot chain; since 2020 legal representative of and taste adviser to Chengdu Tanziyu Catering Management (谭滋鱼)
profile: Tan Changan (谭长安) founded the Tan Yutou fish-head hotpot chain in Chengdu in 1996 and grew it to about 90 restaurants in 58 cities within three years, with revenue above RMB500m by 2002. The original company was later liquidated and its trademarks auctioned in 2021. Since 2020 he has worked on a new venture, Tanziyu, where he says he mainly oversees flavour.
interesting_fact: In 2002 Tan Yutou became the first mainland Chinese hotpot brand to open in Taiwan. At its peak Tan reportedly cut the ribbon at four new restaurants in a single day.
deep_cut_fact: After leaving the army in 1996, he used his RMB5,000 demobilisation payment to open the first Tan Yutou in a small lane near Baihuatan in Chengdu. The 20-odd tables were so busy that people reportedly resold queue tickets.
notes: Hurun listing is from 2007. The original Tan Yutou company has since gone through bankruptcy liquidation, so handle this sensitively and avoid mentioning it in outreach. No published contact found. Restaurant entrepreneur; weak fit with energy/data centers but a strong rise-and-rebuild entrepreneurship story.

name: Stelleo Tolda
current_role: Co-founder and board director (Audit Committee chair), MercadoLibre Inc. (NASDAQ: MELI)
profile: Rio de Janeiro-born Stelleo Tolda co-founded MercadoLibre with Marcos Galperin in 1999 and ran its Brazilian operation (Mercado Livre) from the start. He later served as COO and then President of Commerce, building Latin America's largest e-commerce marketplace. He stepped back from executive duties and since September 2024 has sat on MELI's board, chairing the audit committee since April 2025.
interesting_fact: He met Marcos Galperin in the US while working in New York finance (Merrill Lynch, Lehman Brothers) and helped launch MercadoLibre in Argentina and Brazil the same year, 1999. In 2001 eBay took a stake and formed a five-year alliance with the company.
deep_cut_fact: Before finance he trained as an engineer: he studied mechanical engineering at Stanford, began a master's there, and worked at Silicon Valley tech firms such as Proxim Wireless. He then moved to Banco Icatu and Pactual in Rio.
notes: Now a non-executive director (Ariel Szarfsztejn became CEO on 1 Jan 2026). The deep-cut source is a Brazilian broker blog that also wrongly calls him CEO, so verify the engineering details against MELI proxy bios before use. Best route is MELI IR or a LinkedIn message.

name: Carl M. Eschenbach
current_role: Former CEO of Workday (2022-2026; co-founder Aneel Bhusri is CEO again); director of Palo Alto Networks per SEC filings
profile: Carl Eschenbach is a veteran enterprise-software operator. After sales roles at 3Com, Lucent, Inktomi and EMC, he spent 14 years at VMware (2002-16), rising to President and COO. He then became a partner at Sequoia Capital, joined Workday's board in 2018, was named co-CEO in Dec 2022 and sole CEO in Feb 2024. Workday's leadership page now lists Bhusri as CEO, and Fortune calls Eschenbach 'former Workday CEO'.
interesting_fact: He began as a competitive wrestler and says the sport shaped his business outlook. His leadership motto: 'By serving others, somehow success will follow you.'
deep_cut_fact: His first credential was an Electronics Technician diploma from DeVry, not an elite university degree. He worked his way up through hands-on tech sales roles before running VMware's go-to-market operations.

public_contacts.value: media@workday.com (Workday media relations; he is no longer CEO)

notes: The exact date and terms of his Workday exit were not verified because the web-search budget ran out. Some reports say February 2026, possibly moving to a strategic-adviser role. Palo Alto Networks board seat is from SEC insider data and was not re-verified. The DeVry diploma comes from his former Workday bio (that page no longer renders). Relevant to AI/enterprise-software discussions; Sequoia alumnus.

name: Lawrence Tomlinson
current_role: Chairman, LNT Group (Ginetta Cars, Ideal Carehomes, LNT Construction, LNT Software, LNT Solutions), Leeds
profile: Lawrence Tomlinson (b. 1964, Batley) is an engineer-turned-entrepreneur. In 1988 he bought his parents' single care home and built the Tricare/Orchard Care Homes group, selling it for £175m in 2007. LNT Construction has built roughly a fifth to a quarter of all new UK elderly care homes. He now runs LNT Group, which spans care homes, care software (CoolCare), rail and aviation de-icing chemicals, and Ginetta sports and race cars.
interesting_fact: He won the GT2 class at the 2006 Le Mans 24 Hours driving the Team LNT Panoz Esperante. He also drew up the base specification for the Ginetta G50 race car, which was built in six months.
deep_cut_fact: As a teenager he wrote care-home management software on an Amstrad 8256 for his parents' new care home, the seed of the CoolCare software now used in 1,000+ homes. He bought LNT Solutions, which makes leaf-fall and third-rail de-icing chemicals for Network Rail, from his motor-racing instructor over a pub conversation after a track day.
notes: Was BIS 'Serial Entrepreneur in Residence' in 2013-14 (author of the Tomlinson Report on bank lending to SMEs) and IoD Director of the Year 2013. Holds honorary doctorates from Huddersfield, Bradford and Leeds Met. Sunday Times 2025 put his wealth at £525m. Strong entrepreneurship guest; LNT Solutions offers an energy/infrastructure angle.

name: Zhao Honglin
current_role: Unknown; listed by Hurun (2010) as a Shagang Group shareholder/executive; not on Shagang's current board
profile: Zhao Honglin (赵洪林) appeared on the 2010 Hurun China list with wealth tied to Jiangsu Shagang Group, China's largest private steelmaker (Zhangjiagang), probably as a management shareholder. Shagang's current board (Shen Bin, chairman; Gong Sheng, president) does not include him, and no further public profile was found.
interesting_fact: Shagang reached world attention in 2001 by buying ThyssenKrupp's Dortmund-Hörde steel plant, dismantling it and rebuilding it in China. In 2016 it led the £2.4bn deal for data-centre operator Global Switch.
notes: Identity and current role not confirmed: Baidu blocked access and the web-search budget ran out. The contact is Shagang corporate, not personal. Shagang's Global Switch stake gives a direct data-center angle, but the better podcast target there would be the Shen family.
